DHA may be exposed to greater oxidative damage in the brain, which
creates a heightened level of oxidative stress. A diet rich in vegetables and
fruits provides an array of these powerful antioxidants to protect your brain
and body. Ideally, most of your cooking should be done at low to moderate
temperatures using healthy MUFA fats (monounsaturated fats), including
extra-virgin olive oil, avocado oil, macadamia oil, and walnut oil, and
minimal to modest amounts of omega-6 vegetable oils. When cooking at
high temperatures, use moderate amounts of stable saturated fats, such as
butter, ghee (clarified butter), beef tallow, or duck fat. (Note: although
coconut oil is a saturated fat, it has a moderate smoke point of 350°F and
therefore shouldn’t be used at high temperatures.)
